channel.description: Latest articles from Carolinas' Own Queen City News WJZY-TV (fox46.com)

item.title: Measles outbreak in South Carolina reaches 973 cases
item.description: The South Carolina Department of Public Health has reported 11 new cases of measles, bringing the total to 973, with 105 people in quarantine and 7 in isolation, and potential exposures identified at multiple locations.

item.title: False bomb threat targets Morganton property, suspect wanted
item.description: The Burke County Sheriff's Office responded to a bomb threat at a property in Morganton, but no explosive device was found and an arrest warrant has been issued for John Anthony Pons, Sr. for making the false report.

item.title: Charlotte mayor says changes to I-77 South Express Lanes assigned to the state, invites NCDOT to meeting
item.description: NCDOT secretary apparently told Lyles that there is still time to incorporate community feedback and identify solutions.

item.title: Charlotte shatters temperature record with 83-degree high in February
item.description: Charlotte broke a temperature record on Friday with a high of 83 degrees, but cooler temperatures and scattered showers are expected to return for the weekend, with up to 6 inches of snow possible in the mountains.

item.title: Charlotte FC kicks off 2026 season Saturday against St. Louis City
item.description: In addition to the frontline stars returning, FC’s stalwart in net is back too.

item.title: Fmr. Concord daycare teacher to spend days in jail after hot gluing 3-year-old to seat: Court Docs
item.description: A daycare teacher will spend days in jail for hot gluing a toddler to their seat for not sitting still, according to court records.

item.title: Rumors swirl about ICE facility in Concord; city says no official notice
item.description: The City of Concord announced on Friday that it hasn't heard anything official about a possible federal immigration detention facility coming to the area, following "rumors in the community."

item.title: Charlotte area is home to three of the nation's worst bottlenecks for trucks: Report
item.description: The American Transportation Research Institute has ranked three traffic bottlenecks in the Charlotte area in the top 50, causing significant delays for both trucks and cars during rush hour.

item.title: 'He did what he had to do': Grieving father attacks son’s accused killer inside Mecklenburg courthouse
item.description: A man accused of murder was repeatedly punched and kicked by the father of the victim.

item.title: Charlotte man working to get friend from southwest Asia out of ICE detention facility
item.description: He says his friend has already lost several pounds from lack of food, and his mental health is declining.
